To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Scalable coding is the most suitable for video streaming in a mobile environment and MD coding should be used only in special cases, such as when the mobile devices have very limited battery power or the video stream has very high importance and must be delivered at all costs.
the use of MD and MJPEG coding schemes is beneficial to video streaming in MANETs, but only if the level of mobility of the devices is high and the CPU load is low.
the use of MD coding and MPEG video format is more effective than the use of Scalable coding and MJPEG video format, respectively, in MANET environments with high mobility and low battery life.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: • The effects of mobility on video streaming over MANETs, • The effect of redundancy on video streaming over a MANET, • The effect on battery life of using different coding schemes and different levels of redundancy, and • A comparison of the performance of MPEG and MJPEG video formats over MANETs.
the design and evaluation of scalable and multiple description video streaming over mobile ad hoc networks.
the following questions: (a) What is the impact of the video format and coding schemes on the video quality in a mobile ad hoc network?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of MD and Scalable video coding is not recommended for wireless video transmission in a MANET.
MD coding with MJPEG format and a moderate level of redundancy is more suitable for MANETs.

the use of Scalable Video Coding (SVC) in a Mobile Video Streaming (MVS) over MANET environment is more beneficial and efficient compared to the MD coding scheme, especially when there is a large number of mobile nodes and a low level of redundancy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are proposing a new way of using redundancy in video streaming over MANETs and we are proposing a set of practical solutions for the two scenarios that we have studied.

Scalable video coding is a better choice in a MANET environment than MD coding, and MJPEG is a better choice for video streaming over a MANET than MPEG, and that the level and amount of the redundancy should be carefully selected to achieve the best performance in a given scenario.
Scalable Video Coding (SVC) is a better choice than MD in MANETs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the choice of the right video coding scheme is critical for the performance of the system and that the use of multiple descriptions is a viable solution for video streaming in MANETs, but only if the right amount of redundancy is added.
in order to provide a better quality of service (QoS) for video streaming in MANETs, the use of Scalable coding and MJPEG video format are recommended.
the use of Scalable Video Coding (SVC) is not necessarily the best choice for wireless video streaming over MANETs.
